svg.text: A TEMPERATURE ALONG THE BAND - what the cookie sees, x = machine position (mm)
band position x (mm) - band speed 2.292 mm/s, so 100 mm = 44 s
B WHERE THE HEAT GOES (steady, 900 cookies/h)
C 400 V 3N~ - LOAD PER PHASE (every element on)
E WARM-UP FROM COLD (all elements on)
SF1: E-stop drops the oven feed
Z1 210 C: PID on TC1, 2 s time-proportioning PWM to the SSRs
Z2 200 C: PID on TC2, 2 s time-proportioning PWM to the SSRs
Z3 185 C: PID on TC3, 2 s time-proportioning PWM to the SSRs
Recipe: zones 210 / 200 / 185 C, impingement 70 W/m2K top / 45 through the mesh; bake 265 s = 203 mm
Result (oven.py): core held at >= 95 C for 186 s, water 18% -> 4.6%, top colour index 1.08 (1.0 =
The core sits at 100 C while it still holds water: the heat goes into evaporation (the flat part of
the core curve) - that is why a thin cookie bakes in minutes and the old 20 mm puck never could.
Steady heat 2641 W (2.93 Wh per cookie); installed 4305 W in 9 tubular elements + 3 fans; zone 1
carries 57% - it heats the cold dough and the cold band.
Each element has its own SSR; each zone has a 3-pole C16, a zone contactor KHn whose coil runs through
the zone's STB (SF4, own thermocouple element) and the line contactors K3/K4 (SF1) upstream.
Outer skin <= 38 C (50 mm mineral wool); the puck chain runs under the oven floor and never sees the
All food data are [assumed] - MEASURE on the first bake: dough water, conductivities, the Maillard
constants, and the heat-transfer coefficients of the fans (oven.py header).
